doc.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014

title: Ellington's band, the bandstand as sacred, and the Buddy Catlett and Sonny Payne story
summary: Stories of musicians who fought off the stand but made music together, including Catlett and Sonny Payne sharing a room.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Well the answer is it’s a job for all of us, in all walks of life, whatever you do. Everybody can take it and take the fundamentals and the essence of jazz and apply it. Because sometimes you even hear stories about some of these bands — like I’ve heard somebody tell me some stories about Duke Ellington’s band saying you know nobody in that band got along. I mean I never heard, I might have to do some checking into it further, see a lot © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

of those guys didn’t like each other which is kind of amazing. Because if that was the case, then that too says that look, they understood that even if that was the case, you had some problem with somebody, when they got on the bandstand, that bandstand was sacred. We’re going to take care of business. We’re going to spread the love, and this is the thread that’s going to tie us all together. So that’s a great thing. Music is powerful. I remember one time too, maybe Frank Wess told me this story and then I think Buddy Catlett confirmed it. You know Buddy Catlett was one of the bass players that played with Basie and I knew Buddy Catlett well from my travels in Seattle. But I think Frank told me that one time they were out on the road and Buddy Catlett and whatchacalit, who was the drummer at the time?

Sonny. They shared a room together. And they were good buddies but I guess they both got to drinking. And they got into an argument over something. And he said they just tore up the room. They beat each other up. And the two of them got up the next morning and they had to go make the gig. So I mean the music overrides.

Yeah. Musicians are people too you know, but they had their foibles. It’s funny, the difference that Sonny Payne made in that band, like when you did that thing with your arms. I remember Joe Williams talking about that, that he really lit a fire under that group. Okay I was going to try one more thing for you here.
